summary.name: Homebrew
summary.one_liner: Homebrew is a package manager that installs command-line tools and applications on macOS, Linux and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
use_cases: Installing command-line tools on macOS, Linux or WSL
Installing desktop applications and fonts from the terminal
Keeping a project or machine setup repeatable with a Brewfile
Managing background services with brew services
Deploying Homebrew to many Macs via MDM with the .pkg installer
summary.what_it_does: Homebrew installs command-line tools, libraries, services and applications across macOS, Linux and WSL. It has two package types: formulae, which build tools from upstream source, and casks, which install upstream pre-built binaries such as apps, fonts and plugins. Homebrew Bundle uses a Brewfile to declare desired machine or project state and runs brew bundle to install or update missing and outdated dependencies. Third-party repositories called taps let anyone maintain their own formulae and casks.
notable: Declarative Brewfile-based Homebrew Bundle covering formulae, casks, Mac App Store apps, VSCode extensions, Go, Cargo, uv, Flatpak and more
Formulae in homebrew/core are human-reviewed and must be open source under a Debian Free Software Guidelines-compatible licence
Non-profit, volunteer-run project fiscally hosted by Open Source Collective
Offers a .pkg installer for interactive or unattended MDM installs on macOS
caveats: Some casks auto-update outside Homebrew, so the --greedy flag is needed to update them too
Non-official taps are not reviewed by Homebrew maintainers; the page advises reading how tap trust works first
Requires macOS Sequoia 15 or newer for macOS support, per the page
